seoTitle: How to Add Outlook Calendar to Notion (Link & Embed)
metaDescription: Connect your Outlook or Microsoft 365 calendar to Notion so events, tasks, and schedules show up right inside your workspace.
intro: If your team runs on Outlook for scheduling but Notion for project work, linking the two keeps everything centralized instead of forcing you to check two apps. This guide shows how to bring your Outlook or Microsoft 365 calendar into Notion so events and tasks stay visible in the same place.

steps.heading: Find your Outlook calendar's sharing link
steps.body: In Outlook or Microsoft 365, generate a shareable or embeddable link for the calendar you want to bring into Notion.

steps.heading: Embed the calendar in Notion
steps.body: Use Notion's embed block and paste the Outlook calendar link so it displays as a live calendar view inside your page.

steps.heading: Place it in your workspace or dashboard
steps.body: Position the embedded calendar next to your task lists or project trackers so schedules and work items stay side by side.

steps.heading: Manage events and tasks together
steps.body: Reference Outlook events in your Notion databases where relevant so deadlines line up with what's on your calendar.

steps.heading: Keep both tools updated
steps.body: Continue adding and editing events in Outlook itself — the Notion embed reflects those changes automatically.

faq.question: Do I need a Microsoft 365 subscription for this to work?
faq.answer: You need an Outlook or Microsoft 365 calendar with a shareable link, which is available on most Outlook and Microsoft 365 account types.

faq.question: Can I edit Outlook events from inside Notion?
faq.answer: No, the embed only displays your calendar; edits still need to happen in Outlook or Microsoft 365 directly.

faq.question: Will the embedded calendar refresh with new events?
faq.answer: Yes, since it's a live embed, new or updated Outlook events appear in Notion without any manual re-syncing.

faq.question: Can I add both Outlook and Google Calendar to the same Notion page?
faq.answer: Yes, you can add separate embed blocks for each calendar so multiple schedules show up together on one page.
